**Visual Analysis of Test Image:**
- Sugarcane plant with multiple long, narrow leaves
- **Distinctive longitudinal streaking pattern**: alternating bands of green and pale yellow/tan/straw-colored stripes running parallel to the leaf veins
- The streaks span the full length of multiple leaves
- Lower/older leaves show more complete yellowing and browning (disease progression)
- No discrete spots or focal lesions; pattern is linear and vein-parallel

**Differential Reasoning:**

| Candidate | Match |
|-----------|-------|
| **Streak_Mosaic_Scsmv** | Strong match — characteristic pale/yellow longitudinal streaks parallel to veins across multiple leaves |
| **Sugarcane_Mosaic_Virus** | Possible — but mosaic virus tends to show more patchy/mosaic pattern, less linear |
| **Yellow_Leaf** | Partial — more uniform midrib yellowing expected, not striped |
| **Leaf_Scald** | Less likely — typically shows wavy-margin water-soaked streaks, not uniform banding |
| **Brown_Spot / Yellow_Spot** | No — no discrete spot lesions visible |
| **Pokkah_Boeng** | No — would show shoot distortion/twisting |
| **Grassy_Shoot** | No — would show proliferating grassy shoots |
| **Sett_Rot** | No — affects underground setts, not leaf appearance |

The **continuous, longitudinal pale-yellow streaking parallel to veins** across multiple leaves is the hallmark signature of Streak Mosaic (SCSMV — Sugarcane streak mosaic virus), distinguishing it from the more patchy mosaic of Sugarcane_Mosaic_Virus.
